text:
Leo Tan: hi folks — quick question. Priya and I both work at Redwood and we
re trying to decide how to enroll our family for open enrollment. do we have to put dependents on the same employee's plan or can we split (one person elects employee+spouse, other elects employee+children)?
Priya Singh: adding — we both have similar plans but different payroll impacts. want to split premiums 50/50 if possible. is that allowed?
People Ops: short answer: yes, spouses who are both Redwood employees can each elect coverage, but you cannot double-enroll the same dependent on two employer plans at the company (one plan should be primary). Payroll premium split is possible if you coordinate with benefits admin and payroll; we usually recommend one employee enroll the dependents as primary and the other enrolls as employee-only if they want payroll tax/pre-tax premium benefits.
Leo Tan: ok. example scenario: I enroll employee+children, Priya enrolls employee+spouse. does that count as the children being covered only under mine and spouse coverage under hers? do we get duplicate dental/vision?
Benefits Admin: you can elect overlapping plans (e.g., both elect dental). However, medical plans will coordinate benefits (one primary, one secondary). For premiums: both elections will deduct the applicable premiums from each payroll based on who enrolled. If you want to split a single premium charge (e.g., medical premium for spouse), payroll can accommodate payroll-split contributions if you submit a premium split request form.
Priya Singh: is the premium split form the same as the domestic partner/shared-premium form? where do we find it?
Benefits Bot: Auto-reply: premium split requests require signed authorization from both employees and must be submitted during open enrollment or within 30 days of a qualifying change. Form: https://redwood.example.com/people-ops/forms/premium-split.pdf
Mia (Payroll): technical note: for pre-tax premiums, payroll will only treat amounts deducted from each employee as pre-tax if both deductions comply with cafeteria plan rules. if one employee wants post-tax to cover imputed income reasons (e.g., spouse coverage taxable when spouse has access to employer coverage), thatan be handled but requires us to code it correctly. send the signed form to payroll@redwood.com at least 2 pay cycles before first deduction.
Leo Tan: thanks — what about dependent coverage proof? do we need to upload birth certificates for kids even though both of us work here?
Benefits Admin: yes, dependent documentation is required for initial enrollment: birth certificates or adoption decree, or court guardianship. If both employees already had dependents on file previously, we won't re-request unless the audit flag is triggered. For open enrollment changes we still recommend ensuring docs are uploaded to your HR portal.
Priya Singh: and if we later divorce, how is coverage handled? just to know for long term.
People Ops: in the event of divorce, coverage ends per the QLE rules; you'd have 30 days to elect COBRA for the ex-spouse or enroll dependents under the remaining employee's plan if eligible. Payroll will stop spousal premium deductions on termination date.
Benefits Admin: next steps checklist:
- Decide which employee will be primary for the family medical plan (helps with claims coordination)
- Fill out premium-split authorization if you want payroll to share premium costs
- Upload dependent docs to HR portal (birth certs, marriage cert)
- Submit signed forms to payroll@redwood.com before deductions begin
People Ops: ping us if you'd like someone from Benefits to run a mock-payroll calc so you can see net pay impact.
Priya Singh: please do a mock calc! we
onare about the paperwork timeline, just want to see take-home pay. :)
Mia (Payroll): copying you both — will DM to schedule a quick calc and confirm which pay cycles to target.
Leo Tan: perfect, thanks everyone. leaving thread open until forms submitted. :slightly_smiling_face:
